payload.title: TCP/IP Course in C17
payload.summary: Learn TCP/IP by reading bytes, modeling protocol state, and writing small portable C17 programs across 12 core lessons and four optional Linux labs.

prerequisites: A C17 compiler such as Clang or GCC
Linux or macOS with POSIX APIs for socket lessons
outcomes: Decode protocol bytes without mapping wire data onto C structs
Model bounds, ownership, state transitions, and failure behavior explicitly
Compose parsers and local socket exercises into deterministic diagnostics

items.label: Bytes, Addressing, and Checksums
items.description: Integer representation, byte order, bounds, addresses, and one's-complement checksums.

items.label: Ethernet and ARP
items.description: Local-link framing, MAC addresses, EtherTypes, and address resolution.

items.label: IPv4 Packets
items.description: Header parsing, total length, fragmentation, TTL, and validation.

items.label: ICMP
items.description: Echo messages, error reporting, quoted packets, and checksum handling.

items.label: UDP
items.description: Datagram framing, pseudo-headers, ports, checksums, and loss semantics.

items.label: TCP Segments
items.description: Flags, sequence numbers, options, windows, and segment checksums.

items.label: TCP State and Reliability
items.description: State transitions, acknowledgments, retransmission, flow control, and shutdown.

items.label: Stream Sockets
items.description: POSIX socket lifecycle, partial I/O, loopback, and stream framing.

items.label: DNS
items.description: Names, compression pointers, questions, and resource records.

items.label: HTTP
items.description: Request and response parsing, limits, body framing, and persistent streams.

items.label: Routing and NAT
items.description: Longest-prefix match, forwarding decisions, mappings, and expiry.

items.label: Diagnostics and Integration
items.description: Compose parsers and explain failures across layers from offline fixtures.

allowed: Loopback sockets with operating-system-assigned ephemeral ports
Communication inside one test process or local machine
excluded: Internet access, elevated privileges, packet capture, and raw or packet sockets
Wildcard listeners, TUN/TAP devices, network namespaces, fork, clone, or third-party traffic
Production deployment concerns such as TLS, authentication, event-loop scale, and broad platform abstraction
